acceptanceCriteria: The owned ten-instance scenario creates ten all-role collaboration Runtime instances, routes 20 direct roots and 20 Operation-Wire POSTs arbitrarily, completes 40 durable runs, records zero duplicate attempts, and proves drained workers admit no later work.

The fleet contains one signed internal-protocol-v4 Runtime Build and nine current v5 builds. Compatibility remains separate for schema, wire, Policy/Context, realtime, executable, durable state, and internal protocol; the evidence does not claim arbitrary historical binary compatibility.

Durable admission is tenant-fair and filters incompatible executable digests before LIMIT. A live PostgreSQL case with an unequal four-run/two-run tenant backlog proves a four-item batch interleaves two runs from each tenant. A direct claim rechecks compatibility under the row lock, refuses EXECUTABLE_RETIRED without consuming an attempt, and leaves old work durable for a compatible worker.

Exact PostgreSQL serialization losers in claim and cancellation reaping perform no second transition and leave work for a later poll, while every non-40001 failure still escapes. Startup reconciliation retries the complete repeatable-read transaction from a fresh snapshot after a bounded 1–64 ms full-jitter exponential delay, and the injected loser test proves the application callback runs once.

A run abandoned after its last allowed claim becomes one failed RETRY_EXHAUSTED dead letter, settles its outstanding attempt, appends one failure event, creates no extra attempt, and no longer poisons admission.

The separate manual soak/chaos scenario completes 80 runs in waves across ten instances, abandons and recovers one lease exactly once, replaces three instances, ends with zero failed runs, and records zero post-drain admissions.

The rolling matrix, fanout/worker/reconnect report, and optional-infrastructure absence report connect the BETA-10 fleet to established fanout, fresh-Runtime reconnect, arbitrary-holder reauthorization, and drain evidence. No correctness claim depends on sticky routing, a leader, process registry, cache, broker, Redis, Pusher, WebSocket, or retained connection state.

Gate 8 defines beta.1 drainRuntime as the idempotent local app.close lifecycle transition: it stops new roots and claims, bounds owned work, and disposes the instance. The three durable-run maintenance commands retain Authority, reason, idempotency, expected-version, typed-winner, and audit requirements. A remote drain form requires new Accepted authority for stable Runtime-instance identity, targeting, fencing across process death, and audit.

The five required owned artifacts exist: ten-instance load report, separate soak/chaos report, rolling compatibility matrix, fanout/worker/reconnect report, and optional-infrastructure absence report. Their stable-runner budgets remain separately owned and ordinary changed-loop behavior is unchanged.

The generated application remains under the unchanged 524288-byte bundle ratchet by enabling syntax minification rather than raising the budget. Redis implementation, Pusher/WebSocket, split roles, provider matrix, Studio, and new browser or network administration surfaces remain non-goals.
